title: StockSmart Inventory Finance Standard — Opening Stock Quantity of a New Consigned Bin
content:
This standard of the StockSmart Vendor-Managed Inventory Program fixes the quantity of opening consigned stock placed in a new consigned bin that takes over an item taken out of one of the customer's VendPoint Industrial Vending Program machines.

### Section 1 — the bin

The bin is the consigned bin with the most recent new-bin entry on the program, its fill-to level is the one on that new-bin entry, its reorder point is the highest reorder point any of its par level entries carries, and zero where it has none, and its item is the transferred item; where two or more consigned new-bin entries carry that most recent effective date, or there is none, no opening stock is set under this standard.

### Section 2 — the machine and the visit

The demand machine is the machine of the customer's most recent VendPoint selection removal of the transferred item made at the customer's request; where two or more such removals of the item carry that most recent date, or there is none, no opening stock is set under this standard. The opening stock is placed at the program's service visit dated today; where no service visit is dated today, or two or more are, no opening stock is set under this standard. A row's age in whole months is the number of calendar months from its date to today, less one when today's day of the month is earlier than the row's day of the month.

### Section 3 — the quantity

The opening level is the bin's fill-to level and the carried share is the whole, 1. The opening stock is the opening level times the carried share, which is the product of every share that applies, taken to six decimal places and then rounded down to a whole unit.

### Section 4 — the consigned value cap

The opening stock is placed only while the program's consigned stock value, with the opening stock added, stays at or below the consigned value cap of the program's tier. The program's consigned stock value is its consigned stockings less its consigned consumption, shrink and withdrawals, each at the value it was booked at. The opening stock is valued at the item's contract unit price on its latest price line in the customer's Contract Pricing Agreement, which must be in effect today and alone on its effective date: no price line of the item may take effect after today (every line of the item is dated today or within the 1200 months before it), and no second line may share the latest line's effective date. An item without such a line gets no opening stock under this standard. Where the opening stock worked out in Section 3 would carry the consigned stock value above the cap, it is cut to the whole units that keep the value at or below the cap.

### Worked figures (hypothetical bin and program)

| Fill-to level | Carried share | Opening stock before the cap | Room under the cap | Contract unit price | Units the room allows | Opening stock placed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40 | 1 | 40 | 1000.00 | 12.50 | 80 | 40 |
| 40 | 1 | 40 | 100.00 | 12.50 | 8 | 8 |
| 40 | 1 | 40 | 0.00 or less | 12.50 | 0 | 0 |

The room under the cap is the tier's cap less the program's consigned stock value. The rounding down to whole units comes first; the cap then limits the result to the whole units the room buys at the contract unit price.
